subject: numen (third-party open-source mod)

upstream.author: dwinovo
upstream.licenseSource: META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml in the published jar; the source tree also carries COPYING (GPL-3.0) and LICENSE (LGPL-3.0)
upstream.licenseNote: LGPL obligations are honoured by keeping the upstream license and this record of our changes; we do not relicense or present Numen as our own work.

release.note: Newest published build for Minecraft 1.21.1. It predates upstream HEAD, so it does not contain the newest pathing rework.

head.note: Newest source. No published jar for 1.21.1, so adopting it means building it ourselves.

deployed.note: Upstream 0.1.1 binary with the project patch chain compiled on top. Recorded in manifests/numen-restore.lock.json.

ourChanges.why: Task-local walking with a strict, verified arrival, so the survivor cannot believe it arrived somewhere it did not. The gateway refuses walk_only goto without it.
Restores an existing saved body by its own identity instead of summoning a new one; the survivor reconnect path depends on it.
Keeps the companion body ticking without a client attached.
Keeps the surrounding world ticking while only server-side bodies are present.

capabilityCheck.method: exact identifier search over the decompressed .class/.json/.toml entries of each jar
capabilityCheck.result: None of the five capabilities above are present in the upstream release jar; adopting upstream as-is would break walk_only goto (safe_navigation_unavailable) and body restore.

syncPolicy: Adopt upstream as the baseline and re-apply our capability patches onto it; never drop the patch chain in place. Requires a stopped server, a rebuild of all five capabilities and revalidation of each on the live world.

integration.why: Our use case differs from the upstream default: a server-side autonomous agent with no client attached, requiring strict arrival, restore-by-identity and unattended ticking. Those capabilities are absent from the upstream release, so maintaining them as binary patch deltas over a released jar costs a class-family re-derivation on every sync. Integrating the source gives our changes a defined place and a version to compare against.
integration.authority: Until all five capabilities are folded into the tree and validated on the live world, world/numen-patches/ remains the authoritative build input; afterwards the tree is authoritative and the patches become history plus the capability contract.
integration.status: vendoried; capability fold-in, build and deploy pending a stopped-server window
